newsitem.title: POLAND: HEAVY RAINS FALL ON FLOOD-HIT WESTERN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: HEAVY RAINS FALL ON FLOOD-HIT WESTERN POLAND.

text.p: Heavy rains were falling on Western Poland on Friday morning, including areas already hit by flooding, government crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes said.
"At this moment it is falling, very intensively, from Kolobrzeg (on the Baltic) to Kasprowy (in southern mountains near Zakopane)," Pomes told Reuters at 0900 GMT.

He said the rains were set to be one third as heavy as those which have unleashed almost two weeks of heavy flooding in Poland's south and southwest, but this time the soaked ground was unable to absorb extra water.
"It will be one-third smaller, but even so the danger is a lot greater, because it is not soaking in at all," he said.
"The risk of flooding unfortunately exists," he added.
Pomes said two very intensive storms had just passed over the Leszno and Legnica provinces in the west and southwest.

"The situation is not promising and now all forces and meetings are focussed on minimalising the effects of (any possible) floods, to rescue people and property," he said from crisis committee headquarters in Warsaw.

"The biggest falls are likely to be on Opole on Sunday," he said, referring to a major southwestern city on the Odra river, the centre of which was drowned in up to two metres of water during the first wave of floods.
"It will rain like this until Sunday," he added.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz warned Parliament on Thursday that meteorological services of four countries were 90 percent certain there would be heavy rain threatening possible new floods, but not all forecasters were pessimistic.
Poland's Gazeta Wyborcza daily on Friday quoted the Aura weather service in the Western city of Poznan as saying the rains could quickly move north and pass Poland by.
"These rainfalls will certainly worsen the situation, but there will not necessarily be flooding," Aura official Tadeusz Drozdowski told the newspaper.

The previous rains, falling heavily on the headwaters in the Czech Republic of the major Polish Wisla and Odra rivers, prompted a wave of high water which has been surging north to strike communities including Opole and Wroclaw.
